title: RBC Supports Egale's OUT at Night
description: Add your support at http://outatnight.ca by registering to spend the night outside May 30th or sponsor a team.   For one night, turn your back on comfort and not on our youth.

asr.full_text: For many of us, home provides a sense of belonging and security. But that's not always the case. That is why RBC is proud to support a Gals Out at Night,. A national campaign to raise funds and awareness for LGBTQ2S homeless youth. Well, because it could have been me on the streets. It could have been, if my parents had acted any differently,. Me, homeless, with nowhere to go. Adolescence is a time when people tend to feel alienated anyway. They've got hormones bursting out all over the place and they assume it's only them. So when you are only a very small minority compared to the rest of your peers, there's. Even more isolation that can happen. And when you're isolated and you don't feel supported or you feel threatened, then you tend to run. So I think that's why. It's adolescence times 10 for these kids. Just be open and listen. Everyone comes with their own views on what it means. But really, I think being just supportive to your family member or co-worker is critically important to helping that person come through the journey of coming out. I absolutely believe it's important to have allies because without allies, that leaves just the people in the community. And you need more people than that. You need as many people as possible. You need society in general to come together for a cause such as this, and any cause really. It can't be left to just the individual groups who need the support. If there is a way to raise awareness of LGBT youth homelessness. And what less fortunate people have to deal with in our community, then we should take it. Let's all rally to support Out at Night on May 30th to end youth homelessness in the LGBTQ2S community. This is our call to action. Thank you.
